sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's energy transition hinges on PLN's capex cycle and feed-in tariff revisions, making policy clarity the dominant swing factor for local renewables valuations.
US solar demand is structurally supported by IRA subsidies and grid-scale backlog, insulating SEDG/ENPH from near-term rate volatility.
Climate-tech capital is bifurcating: US equipment makers benefit from reshoring incentives, while Indonesian developers face currency and offtake risks that cap upside.
sectors.ai: US-listed renewables rebounded on rate-cut hopes while Indonesian names lagged on rupiah weakness and policy uncertainty. Buy US solar equipment (SEDG, ENPH) for near-term beta, but rotate into Indonesian utilities (HGII) only after clarity on PLN procurement and tariff reform. Hedge IDR exposure via NRG-style cash-flow names.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rupiah depreciation and US dollar-linked earnings are the primary alpha driver, rewarding exporters like POLU and AMMS while pressuring import-heavy domestic FMCG margins.
Middle-class consumption is bifurcating: premium/health-oriented brands (BIKE, AGAR) capture wallet share, while mass-market staples face volume stagnation due to weak purchasing power.
Regulatory and halal-certification tailwinds are consolidating the sector, favoring compliant, well-capitalized players (VISI, AEGS) and squeezing smaller informal competitors.
sectors.ai: Buy selective momentum names (BIKE, POLU, AGAR) on short-term liquidity-driven rallies, but trim exposure into strength as aggregate sector weakness (-0.83%) signals rotation out of staples. Favor exporters with US dollar earnings (POLU, AMMS) over domestic-demand plays; hold cash for pullback entries near support.
